title: CLR/64/2015 of Vijay Kumar Gupta Vs Ambrish Kumar Agarwal AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 64/2015
Vijay Kumar Gupta Ö. Revisionist

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate, for the revisionist.
Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate, for the
respondents.
By means of this revision, the judgment and
order dated 14.5.2015 passed by the District Judge, Pauri
Garhwal has been assailed whereby the SCC Suit No.
4/2013, presented for the recovery of arrears of rent and
eviction, was dismissed.
Having heard learned Counsel for the parties, it
transpires that the building is quite old. The Court is not
inclined to enter into the discussion regarding the
dilapidated condition of the said building, but the finding of
the learned Court below is certainly infirm for the reason
that the learned Trial Judge has given the finding that the
suit was not presented by Smt. Sita Gupta, the mother of
the plaintiff, who was another co-owner of the demised
premises, and it was initiated only by Mr. Vijay Kumar
Gupta. This finding is infirm because it is the law, as has
been accepted since time immemorial, that any of the co-landlords can initiate the proceedings of eviction. All the
landlords need not to join while launching such
proceedings and more for the reason that the plaintiff has
proved in his evidence that on account of the family
settlement, such demised premises was put to his share.

2
It also transpires that Mr. Ambrish Kumar
Agarwal is an old tenant in such residential premises. So, it
can be assumed that in such old times, the rent had been
much meagre and now, with the passage of time, the rate
of such rent has enhanced. As per the version of the
landlord, it became Rs. 700/- per month after the death of
plaintiffís father Mr. Ram Gopal Gupta way back in early
1980s.
I think the rate of rent at such an exorbitant
denomination in a small town like Kotdwar is hardly
believable and that too in those olden times. So, the version
of the tenant/defendant that the rate of rent was Rs. 300/-
per month is more credible.
At the same time, it is certain that the defendant
has been in the arrears of rent. He was quite negligent and
committed repeated lapse in paying the regular rent and
observing the discipline by not making such payments to
the landlord. So, a notice terminating his tenancy was
issued on 15.11.2012, which was received by the tenant
and it was replied on 21.12.2012.
Learned Counsel of the defendant respondent
has drawn the attention of this Court towards the paper
no. 9Ga to show that after the initiation of the SCC Suit No.
4/2013, the whole rent and other dues required under
Section 20(4) of the U.P. Rent Control Act was deposited by
the tenant on 27.5.2013.
Even if it is accepted for a moment, then also the
fact remains that Mr. Ambrish Kumar Agarwal has got
constructed his own residence at Shivalik Nagar, Kotdwar,
as has been accepted by him in his cross-examination
dated 12.5.2014 in paragraphs 10 and 12 of such
examination. It has been accepted in so many happy words
that he has got constructed his own house at Shivalik

3
Nagar and his family members reside there. However, his
version that on account of his heart and kidney ailments,
he is residing in the demised premises is hardly believable
and is rejected for the reason that at the age of 72 years on
the date of his cross-examination on 12.5.2014, it is
unacceptable for such an aged man not to leave along with
his son, daughter, grandchildren and other family members
and reside alone and separately in the demised premises.
That apart, in the bank accounts of Mr. Ambrish
Kumar Agarwal, his address has also been displayed to be
of Shivalik Nagar, Kotdwar. So, it leaves no room for doubt
that he does not leave in the demised premises and wants
to retain the same for the reasons best known to him.
In that way, he is not entitled to the benefit of
Section 20(4) of the U.P. Rent Control Act in view of the
proviso of such sub-section, which reads as under:
ìProvided that nothing in this sub-section, shall
apply in relation to a tenant who or any member
of whose family has built or has otherwise
acquired in a vacant state, or has got vacated
after acquisition, any residential building in the
same city, municipality, notified area or town
area.î
I am of the view that the impugned judgment
suffers from infirmity. Hence, revision is allowed. Impugned
judgment and order is set aside. The suit is decreed for
eviction. However, this Court is not inclined to accept the
rate of rent to be Rs. 700/- per month. Tenant/respondent
shall immediately vacate the house and will forthwith hand
over the peaceful and vacant possession of the same to the
plaintiff appellant. LCR be sent back.
